name: dose-input
title: Dose Input
description: Flags ISMP error-prone dose designations as typed (trailing zeros, missing leading zero, U and IU, µg, cc, a unit flush against the number, uncommaed large numbers), rewrites the dose safely, offers the likely value when 10× outside the usual range and spells it back.

meta.summary: Flags error-prone dose notation as it is typed and doses ten times outside the usual range, so a slipped decimal isn't read as a ten-fold dose.
meta.server: Validate doses against the prescribing system's drug database and require clinical review; this field is a typing aid.
catches: Trailing zeros (1.0 mg) and missing leading zeros (.5 mg)
Error-prone abbreviations: U, IU, µg, cc
A unit typed flush against the number, and large numbers without separators
Doses 10× outside the range you pass (mg typed for mcg, a slipped decimal)
The dose spelled back in words
limits: Not a clinical decision tool: it does not know the patient, the drug or safe dosing
Range checks only work with the range you supply
Not a medical device; dosing must be checked by a qualified professional
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-describedby to an aria-live="polite" hint
aria-invalid when the dose can't be read
Fixes and suggested values are buttons with visible text, returning focus to the input

sources.label: ISMP List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations

rules.note: Informational, not medical advice. Checked that the ISMP list covers trailing and missing leading zeros, U, IU and µg. Not every flagged pattern was matched line by line.
